issues.legal_issue: An inter vivos endowment is effective upon the owner's declaration, and the founder's retention of the office of manager does not by itself prevent its creation.
material_facts: The owner executed and registered a deed dedicating the disputed property to a mosque and madrasa.
The deed allowed the owner to remain in possession as the first mutawalli, with his wife to succeed him.
The challengers did not discharge the burden of proving that the deed was sham, fictitious, or not intended to operate as an endowment.
issues.conclusion: The endowment was validly created and was not shown to be a sham or illusory transaction.
issues.legal_principle: A wakf inter vivos is completed by the owner's declaration of endowment. The founder may appoint himself the first mutawalli, and where the founder and mutawalli are the same person, physical transfer of possession or a change in the property's recorded ownership is unnecessary. An apparent transaction is presumed real, and the person alleging that it was not intended to operate as a wakf bears the burden of proving that claim. The judgment relies on Mulla's Principles of Mahomedan Law, 16th Edition, Article 186; it cites no earlier court decision on this point.

rule.if: inter_vivos_endowment_dispute and owner_declared_dedication and founder_retained_management and challenger_failed_to_prove_sham

predicates.inter_vivos_endowment_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an owner created an endowment during the owner's lifetime.
predicates.owner_declared_dedication: The owner declared that identified property was dedicated to a religious or charitable purpose.
predicates.founder_retained_management: The owner retained or assumed management of the dedicated property after making the declaration.
predicates.challenger_failed_to_prove_sham: A person challenging the endowment did not prove that the declaration was fictitious or not intended to operate.

issues.definition: When an owner declares a dedication and retains management, the endowment is effective if a challenger fails to prove it was a sham.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to provide endowment accounts under statutory requirements does not establish that no endowment was created where no accounts were in fact written and the endowment provides a current benefit to the founder or the founder's family.
material_facts: The challengers relied on the alleged failure to furnish particulars and accounts under the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, 1923, as evidence that no wakf had been created.
The High Court found that no account books had ever been written.
The deed provided for the founder and his wife to maintain themselves from the property's income during their lifetimes.
issues.conclusion: The alleged failure to comply with the accounting requirements did not show that the endowment was not created.
issues.legal_principle: The contention based on Sections 8 and 10 of the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, 1923, failed because the High Court found that no account books had been written. The judgment also refers to Mulla's Mahomedan Law, 12th Edition, Article 171A, for the proposition that the Act did not apply to a wakf under which a benefit was for the time being claimable by the wakif or a family descendant. No earlier court case is cited on this contention.

rule.if: endowment_validity_dispute and statutory_accounting_failure_alleged and no_account_books_were_written and current_benefit_reserved_for_founder_or_family

predicates.endowment_validity_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a religious or charitable endowment was created.
predicates.statutory_accounting_failure_alleged: A challenger alleges that required particulars or accounts were not furnished.
predicates.no_account_books_were_written: No account books were ever prepared for the endowment's income or expenditure.
predicates.current_benefit_reserved_for_founder_or_: The endowment allows a current benefit to be claimed by its founder or a member of the founder's family.

issues.definition: An alleged failure to furnish accounts does not disprove an endowment when no account books were written and a current benefit is reserved for the founder or family.

issues.legal_issue: A deed identifying a religious institution by a general description is not void for uncertainty when other evidence from the donor identifies the institution intended.
material_facts: The deed referred generally to the mosque and madrasa in the locality, where there was more than one mosque.
A later document executed by the donor identified the intended mosque as Barhi Masjid and identified the madrasa.
The donor was in a position to know which mosque and madrasa the deed intended to benefit.
issues.conclusion: The deed was not void for uncertainty because the intended mosque and madrasa could be identified.
issues.legal_principle: A dedication is not uncertain merely because its description, read alone, could refer to more than one institution if other evidence identifies the intended beneficiary. The court relied on the donor's later identification of the institutions; it cited no earlier case on this point.

predicates.endowment_dispute: The proceeding concerns the validity of a dedication to a religious or charitable institution.
predicates.deed_describes_beneficiary_generally: The deed describes the intended beneficiary in terms that could refer to more than one institution.
predicates.donor_later_identified_intended_institut: A later statement or document by the donor identifies the institution intended by the deed.

issues.definition: A general description of a beneficiary is not uncertain when the donor later identifies the institution intended.

issues.legal_issue: The possession claim was not barred by the limitation provision invoked where the suit was filed less than six years after the donor's death.
material_facts: The donor died only a few months after executing the documents on which the purchasers relied.
The suit was filed in 1955, less than six years after the donor's death.
The challengers relied on Article 142 of the Limitation Act.
issues.conclusion: Article 142 did not apply to bar the suit on these facts.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that Article 142 of the Limitation Act was inapplicable on the facts, noting that the suit was filed within six years after the donor's death. No earlier case is cited for this conclusion.

predicates.possession_claim_limitation_challenge: The proceeding includes a challenge that a claim for possession is time-barred.
predicates.suit_filed_soon_after_donor_death: The suit was instituted less than six years after the donor died.

issues.definition: A possession claim is not barred under the invoked limitation rule when the suit was instituted less than six years after the donor died.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court must remand for determination of possession and mesne-profit relief when the trial court did not decide those issues and the appellate judgment does not make clear whether the relief was properly available.
material_facts: The trial court's listed issues included recovery of possession and mesne profits, but its judgment did not decide those issues.
The High Court granted possession and mesne profits after finding that the purchasers had no title, but did not address whether the trial court had left those prayers undecided or abandoned.
The judgment referred to statutory provisions under which an eviction decree could, at the relevant time, be made only by the appointed Controller.
issues.conclusion: The matter was remanded to the High Court to determine the relevant issue, particularly the prayers for eviction and mesne profits.
issues.legal_principle: Where the record leaves unresolved whether relief was abandoned or whether the court granting it had authority to do so, the matter should be remitted for determination. The court referred to Sections 11 and 18 of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947, concerning the Controller's authority over eviction. No earlier case is cited.

predicates.appeal_from_appellate_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a judgment that granted relief after reversing a lower court.
predicates.trial_court_did_not_decide_possession_or: The trial court did not determine the claims for possession or mesne profits.
predicates.appellate_basis_for_grant_is_unclear: The appellate judgment does not resolve whether those claims were abandoned or otherwise properly before the court.
predicates.eviction_authority_is_reserved_to_specia: The governing arrangement assigns authority to order eviction to a designated officer rather than the court granting the decree.

issues.definition: When the trial court left possession and mesne-profit claims undecided, the appellate basis for granting them is unclear, and eviction authority is assigned to a special officer, the unresolved relief issue is remanded for determination.
